entries.definition: engaged in or accustomed to close observation
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The baseline of the family - close observation stated flatly, with none of the danger *vigilant* keeps in view.
examples: caught by a couple of alert cops
alert enough to spot the opportunity when it came
constantly alert and vigilant, like a sentinel on duty

entries.definition: carefully observant or attentive; on the lookout for possible danger
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The grandest word here, promising watch so total that no possible danger slips past, where *open-eyed* claims only that the eyes are open.

entries.definition: (British informal) not to be deceived or hoodwinked
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: British informal, and it praises a different sharpness - not watching for danger but being too knowing to be taken in.

entries.definition: fully alert and watchful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Brisk and informal, it compresses full alertness into a word you could clap someone on the shoulder with, where *vigilant* keeps it solemn.

entries.definition: always watchful
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Unsettling as much as admiring - watchfulness pictured as an eye that never closes, where *sleepless* says only that the watch never stops.
examples: to an eye like mine, a lidless watcher of the public weal

entries.definition: carefully observant or attentive; on the lookout for possible danger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest member - it names the posture of careful attention and looking out for danger without commending it the way *vigilant* does.

entries.definition: always watchful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the cost in view: the watch is unbroken, at a price of rest that *watchful* never has to pay.

entries.definition: carefully observant or attentive; on the lookout for possible danger
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and dutiful: attentiveness owed rather than merely shown, with the possible danger always in the frame.
examples: the vigilant eye of the town watch

entries.definition: carefully observant or attentive; on the lookout for possible danger
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest of the danger-watching words - attention that is simply not asleep to what may be coming, well short of *argus-eyed*'s all-seeing claim.

entries.definition: engaged in or accustomed to close observation
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Shares *alert*'s definition but leans on the habit end of it - observation kept up rather than switched on.

entries.definition: fully alert and watchful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds completeness to *alert* and little else - the force is all in the fully, with nothing left dozing.

entries.definition: frightening because of an awareness of danger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest force here — fear pinned to a danger you can recognise, which makes it a warning rather than the sheer horror of *horrifying*.

entries.definition: causing consternation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Consternation at full weight — it knocks the composure sideways, where *dismaying* only unsettles it.

entries.definition: provoking horror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns as much as it describes — the horror is charged to the thing as a fault, where *horrifying* only reports the effect.

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Broad and unspecific — it names the terror without picturing it, where *fearsome* gives the thing a shape.

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grave and flat, treating the terror as a settled fact of the situation with none of the flourish of *direful*.
examples: a career or vengeance so direful that London was shocked

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heightened form, reaching for a weight that *dire* carries without effort.
examples: a career or vengeance so direful that London was shocked

entries.definition: causing consternation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentler consternation: spirits sink rather than reel, and the thing is not condemned outright as *appalling* condemns it.

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Elevated, almost ceremonial — the terror is stated as an attribute the thing simply has, not an effect it works on you.
examples: the dread presence of the headmaster
polio is no longer the dreaded disease it once was

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The participle turns the fear around: the thing is defined by the dread already aimed at it, where *dreadful* says it causes dread.
examples: polio is no longer the dreaded disease it once was

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says plainly that the thing causes dread — the workaday partner to *dread*'s elevation.

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Points outward at what causes the fear rather than inward at whoever feels it, the opposite reading to the one the word's shape invites.

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Concedes stature to what frightens — the terror it names is formidable, not merely nasty as in *horrible*.

entries.definition: provoking horror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Fright rather than full horror — the same sense worn lightly enough to sound almost decorous beside *horrifying*.

entries.definition: provoking horror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, all-purpose word for the quality — it states the horror without staging it.
examples: war is beyond all words horrible

entries.definition: provoking horror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps the verb's live action, the thing doing the horrifying to you as you watch, where *horrible* merely names the quality.

entries.definition: provoking horror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Nothing to do with looks here: a blunt, unadorned word for what provokes horror, and the flatness is the whole of its force.

entries.definition: pertaining to unconventional choices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats the unconventionality as something chosen, and a choice is describable without being deplored.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strong and faintly appalled — the oddity is loud enough to unsettle, not merely to be noticed.
examples: restaurants of bizarre design — one like a hat, another like a rabbit

entries.definition: marked by a carefree unconventionality or disreputableness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts its weight on the carefreeness itself, which is what the word names whether the result reads as dash or as disrepute.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most tolerant reading of the same conspicuous oddity, allowing it to be indulged where *freakish* will not.

entries.definition: (informal) strikingly unconventional
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal, and the striking quality lands as a thrill rather than a fault — the approving end of a family whose middle condemns.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The variant spelling of *flaky*, carrying the identical shrug at strangeness that will not be weighed.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and dismissive — the oddity is treated as too insubstantial to be taken seriously.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pushes the strangeness toward the unnatural, so the deviation sounds like a defect of kind rather than a quirk.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The informal, offhand counterpart to *freakish*, registering the strangeness as a jolt rather than a fault.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and almost relishing — the same conspicuous excess sounds enjoyed here, where *freakish* deplores it.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and blunt, putting the oddity outside any expected range without making it a flaw of character.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The strangeness is excessive to the edge of absurdity, and the word scorns it where *eccentric* would indulge it.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and cool, naming the same conspicuous strangeness with a raised eyebrow instead of *outlandish*'s scorn.

entries.definition: marked by a carefree unconventionality or disreputableness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Tilts toward the disreputable half of the sense, though the carefreeness keeps it amused rather than condemning.
examples: a cocktail party given by some … raffish bachelors

entries.definition: marked by a carefree unconventionality or disreputableness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Hears dash in the same carefree disrepute that *raffish* hears a shabbiness in.

entries.definition: not conventional or conformist
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat, judgement-free naming of the departure itself, which *bizarre* and *outlandish* charge up into a verdict.

entries.definition: having a body or a body of a specified kind; often used in combination
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The unmarked base of the set - it says only that a body is there, or that one of a stated kind is, and waits for a word in front of it to say which.

entries.definition: invested with a bodily form especially of a human body
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The one member that treats embodiment as something conferred rather than measured, and it carries a gravity the shape words never reach for.
examples: a monarch … regarded as a god incarnate

entries.definition: having a lithe body
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises suppleness rather than outline - where *slim-bodied* reports a shape, this admires the ease of one.

entries.definition: having a relatively long body
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pure measurement along a single axis, and a comparative one at that - it reports length against other bodies without admiring or faulting it.

entries.definition: having a relatively narrow body
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures across where *long-bodied* measures along, and is just as uncommitted about whether narrowness is a virtue.
